getUserTypesCharFunction(userTypes)

 

Create a characteristic function of user types.

This function returns a 2-tuple where the first element is the (characteristic) function determining if an obj's user type belongs to userTypes. If userTypes is c{None}, the function returns c{true}. The second element of the returned tuple is an immutable collection of user types in c{userTypes} or c{None} if userTypes is c{None}.

Parameters:
  • userTypes (maybe(string | Iterable(string))) - The given user type(s).
Returns: tuple(callable, maybe(Iterable(string)))
Return a 2-tuple where the first element is a function determining if an object's user type belongs to userTypes and the second element is an immutable collection of user types.

popFirstElem(it)

 

Pop off the first element of an iterator in a safe way.

Safe, here, means that if the iterator is empty, a GeoError exception is raised in stead of a StopIteration exception. Since the next method of an iterator should not be called directly (it can cause for-loops higher up to terminate to early, silently!), and since the railyard API:s often returns iterables, even in cases where one typically is interested only in the first element, this method is convenient.

Parameters:
  • it (Iterable(any)) - Any iterable
Returns: any
The first element of it (it also gets consumed if it is an iterator).
Decorators:
  • @typedoc
